### Load Libraries

```{r}
#| output: false
library(terra)
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)
library(kableExtra)
library(sf)
library(stars)
```

### Load in the Data

```{r}
#| output: false
# Raster for bathymetry
bathymetry <- rast(
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/depth.tif"
)

# Shapefile for West Coast EEZ
eez <- st_read(
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/wc_regions_clean.shp"
)

# Combine SST rasters into one layered raster
file_paths <- c(
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/average_annual_sst_2008.tif",
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/average_annual_sst_2009.tif",
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/average_annual_sst_2010.tif",
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/average_annual_sst_2011.tif",
  "/Users/cuvlin/Documents/MEDS/eds223/eds223-hw3-where-are-the-abalone/data/average_annual_sst_2012.tif"
)
sst_08_12 <- rast(file_paths)
```

### Process Data

```{r}
#| output: false
# Create 5-year average SST raster (2008-2012)
sst_5yr_mean <- app(sst_08_12, fun = mean)

# Convert from kelvin to celsius (subtract 273.15)
sst_5yr_mean <- sst_5yr_mean - 273.15

# Crop the extent of the depth raster to the extent of the SST raster
bathymetry <- crop(bathymetry, ext(sst_5yr_mean))

# Check the resolution of both rasters
print(c(res(bathymetry), res(sst_5yr_mean)))

# Resample the depth data to match that of SST
bathymetry_resample <- resample(bathymetry, sst_5yr_mean, method = "bilinear")
```

```{r}
#| output: false
# Check to see if the resolution, extent, and crs are the same
# Check CRS
same.crs(bathymetry_resample, sst_5yr_mean)

# Check extent
ext(bathymetry_resample) == ext(sst_5yr_mean)

# Check resolution
res(bathymetry_resample) == res(sst_5yr_mean)
```

### Find suitable locations

I am going to reclassify the data into suitable habitats as `1`, and unsuitable habitats as `0` for both depth and temperature.

```{r}
#| output: false
# Reclassify depth
rcl_depth <- matrix(
  c(1, Inf, 0, -70, 0, 1, -Inf, -70, 0),
  ncol = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)
depth_suitability <- as.factor(classify(bathymetry_resample, rcl = rcl_depth))

# Reclassify SST
rcl_sst <- matrix(
  c(-Inf, 11, 0, 11, 30, 1, 30, Inf, 0, NaN, NaN, 0),
  ncol = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)
sst_suitability <- as.factor(classify(sst_5yr_mean, rcl = rcl_sst))
```

Now im gonna find areas where both rasters are equal to 1. Then I will vectorize to turn it into a shaepfile I can use SF functions on.

```{r}
#| output: false
# Find where both areas are equal to 1 (suitable habitatas in depth and temp)
suitable_habitats <- as.int(sst_suitability == 1 & depth_suitability == 1)

# Vectorize data
suit_hab_vector <- st_as_sf(as.polygons(
  suitable_habitats,
  aggregate = FALSE
)) |>
  filter(mean == 1)
```

### Determine the most suitable EEZ

```{r}
# Area per pixel
pixel_area <- (res(suitable_habitats)[1] * 111.1) *
  (res(suitable_habitats)[2] * 111.1)
# Combine geometries
habitat_eez_area <- st_join(eez, suit_hab_vector) |>
  summarize(n_pixels = sum(mean), .by = rgn, across(geometry, st_union)) |>
  mutate(total_area = n_pixels * pixel_area)
tm_shape(habitat_eez_area) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "total_area",
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Total Suitable Habitat Area (km^2)")
  ) +
  tm_title(
    text = "EEZ Classified by Total Suitable Habitat area for Oyster Aquaculture",
    size = 1.75
  )
```

### Turning it into a function and using it for Abalone

I am going to turn all the above code into a function, and then use the function for mapping suitable Abalone habitats.

#### For Abalone

| Factor | Minimum | Maximum |
|:-------|:-------:|--------:|
| Depth  |   0m    |     54m |
| Temp   |   15C   |     25C |

### Define Function

As specified in the homework assignment, the arguments for the function will be min depth, max depth, min temperature, max temperature, and species name.

```{r}
#| output: false
#| warning: false
# Define Function
map_species_habitat <- function(
  min_depth,
  max_depth,
  min_temp,
  max_temp,
  species_name
) {
  # Reclassify depth
  rcl_depth <- matrix(
    c(min_depth, Inf, 0, -max_depth, min_depth, 1, -Inf, -max_depth, 0),
    ncol = 3,
    byrow = TRUE
  )
  depth_suitability <- as.factor(classify(bathymetry_resample, rcl = rcl_depth))

  # Reclassify SST
  rcl_sst <- matrix(
    c(-Inf, min_temp, 0, min_temp, max_temp, 1, max_temp, Inf, 0, NaN, NaN, 0),
    ncol = 3,
    byrow = TRUE
  )
  sst_suitability <- as.factor(classify(sst_5yr_mean, rcl = rcl_sst))

  # Find where both areas are equal to 1 (suitable habitatas in depth and temp)
  suitable_habitats <- as.int(sst_suitability == 1 & depth_suitability == 1)

  # Vectorize data
  suit_hab_vector <- st_as_sf(as.polygons(
    suitable_habitats,
    aggregate = FALSE
  )) |>
    filter(mean == 1)

  # Area per pixel
  pixel_area <- (res(suitable_habitats)[1] * 111.1) *
    (res(suitable_habitats)[2] * 111.1)

  # Combine geometries
  habitat_eez_area <- st_join(eez, suit_hab_vector) |>
    summarize(n_pixels = sum(mean), .by = rgn, across(geometry, st_union)) |>
    mutate(total_area = n_pixels * pixel_area)

  # Map
  my_map <- tm_shape(habitat_eez_area) +
    tm_polygons(
      fill = "total_area",
      fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Total Suitable Habitat Area (km^2)")
    ) +
    tm_title(
      text = paste(
        "EEZ Classified by Total Suitabe Habitat Area for ",
        species_name,
        "Aquaculture"
      ),
      size = 1.75
    )
  return(my_map)
}
```

Use function to map suitable Abalone Habitats: We know the specific values from the table above

```{r}
#| warning: false
map_species_habitat(0, 54, 11, 25, "Abalone")
```
